description: Oh no! Your putty knife sinks right into the trim. It's basically wet bread.
option_1: Replace all the exterior trim on the house

description: Trim off, and the plywood underneath is dark and crumbly. It's been wet for a long time.
option_1: Spray it with bleach and cover it up
option_2: Cut out and patch the sheathing

description: Mystery solved: there's no flashing above the window. Water has been walking right in.
option_1: Run a bigger bead of caulk on top
option_2: Install flashing tape and a drip cap
option_3: Add an awning over every window

description: The window frame is soft at the corners. This window may be beyond saving.
option_1: Replace every window in the house

description: The sill is cracked and holding a little puddle. It's a tiny swimming pool for bugs.
You can feel a breeze through a finger-wide gap around the frame.
option_3: Fill it with regular expanding foam

description: The test swab turned red. The trim paint has lead.
option_2: Sand it off with a power sander
option_3: Hire a hazmat crew for the whole house

description: This window looks amazing. Every other window now looks sad by comparison.
option_2: Caulk over the old caulk on all of them right now

description: Your partner yells up: "While you're on the ladder, the gutters are overflowing!"
option_1: Install gutter guards on the whole house
option_2: Lean the ladder on the gutter and reach
option_3: Clean the gutter by this window

description: The store's trim looks nothing like your 1950s trim. It's modern. Too modern.
option_1: Have a millwork shop match the profile
option_3: Replace the trim on every window to match

description: Behind the bad sheathing, the stud next to the window is soft too.
option_3: Fill the rot with expanding foam

description: Your window is 31 3/8 inches wide. No store carries that. Custom order: 8 weeks.
option_1: Reframe the opening to a standard size
option_2: Order a custom window and protect the opening
option_3: Jam in a standard window with lots of shims

description: Pulling the outside sill cracks the interior window stool. Now it's an inside job too.
option_2: Redo all the interior window trim

description: After foaming the gap, the window won't open. The frame bowed just a little.
option_2: Trim back the foam and adjust the shims
option_3: Force it open with a pry bar

description: A breeze carries lead paint chips straight into the vegetable garden.
option_1: Stop work, clean up, and test the soil

description: The clean window makes the yellowed blinds look like they lost a fight.
option_1: Take them down and tape up a bedsheet
